paper.title: Some new criteria for the uniqueness of limit cycles in Rayleigh--Lienard systems
paper.abstract: In this paper, new uniqueness criteria for Rayleigh--Li\'enard systems with damping of positive odd degree in the velocity are established. Under suitable conditions, any limit cycle is unique and hyperbolic, with its stability determined by the damping signs. Neither symmetry nor monotonicity of the damping and restoring functions is required. Changes of variables and time yield further criteria for generalized Kukles systems. Applications to three polynomial families yield uniqueness and nonexistence results. In particular, we resolve an open uniqueness problem for a hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator left open by Chen et al. (Phys. D, 2021). We also give an alternative uniqueness proof for a system with homogeneous components and obtain uniqueness and nonexistence results for a modified hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is planar limit-cycle uniqueness for oscillator equations, without a central entropy, dimension, symbolic or group-action theme.

paper.title: Flocking with finite communication speed: a Doppler-inspired Lyapunov approach
paper.abstract: We study the Cucker--Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays arising from finite-speed information propagation. Our main contribution is a Lyapunov functional inspired by the Doppler effect, combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction involving the receiver velocity. Its dissipation yields uniform delay bounds without relying on velocity contraction estimates. For two agents in one spatial dimension, we prove asymptotic flocking for arbitrary compatible subluminal initial histories, assuming only that the influence function has a divergent integral at infinity. A bounded geometric correction extends this result to arbitrary spatial dimension when all values of the initial velocity histories lie on one common affine line. For multiple agents in one dimension, we obtain uniform delay bounds, and thus flocking, provided that a fixed agent is leftmost for all sufficiently large times. In all these flocking regimes, the spatial diameter remains uniformly bounded and the velocity diameter decays exponentially. We also derive a conditional criterion involving logarithmic sums when the leftmost agent changes infinitely often. Finally, we construct a multidimensional analogue of the Doppler-inspired functional and identify an additional assumption needed to obtain delay bounds in the general case.

analysis.relevance_note: This is an applied flocking and delay-stability study, without a central connection to the strongest profile themes.

paper.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
paper.abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.

analysis.relevance_note: Maximizing measures and countable symbolic systems directly match ergodic optimization and symbolic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive potential families on countable-alphabet subshifts. Coercivity prevents maximizing sequences from losing mass to large symbols.
analysis.problem: Establish existence of maximizing measures in a noncompact symbolic setting.
analysis.main_result: On a closed countable-alphabet subshift, upper semicontinuous bounded-above potentials in a subadditive or almost-additive family admit maximizing measures under the stated coercivity condition on the first potential. Every maximizing sequence is uniformly tight. The coercivity condition is not formulated explicitly. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Uniform tightness of maximizing sequences from coercivity
analysis.context: Ergodic optimization for noncompact symbolic systems.

paper.title: Some remarks on polynomial vector fields in $\RR^2$
paper.abstract: In this paper, we study planar polynomial vector fields admitting invariant circles. We characterize polynomial vector fields having $m$ concentric invariant circles, and we describe those having three invariant circles whose centers are not collinear. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for the unit circle to be the unique limit cycle of a quadratic vector field. We prove that a cubic or quartic Kolmogorov vector field having the unit circle invariant has no circular limit cycle, and that a quartic vector field with two concentric circular limit cycles has at most three circular limit cycles, this bound being sharp.

analysis.relevance_note: This concerns circular invariant sets and limit-cycle bounds of polynomial ODEs, without a central profile theme.

paper.title: On the stability of rank-one factors for Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions
paper.abstract: We prove $C^1$-stability of $C^\infty$ rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently $C^1$-small $C^\infty$ perturbation of the action will also have a $C^\infty$ rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the $C^1$-stability of the product structure for Anosov $\mathbb Z^2$-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two $\mathbb Z$-Anosov actions.

analysis.relevance_note: Factors and stability of higher-rank group actions are directly central to the profile.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove persistence of smooth rank-one factors under small continuously differentiable perturbations of certain higher-rank Anosov actions. A consequence is stability of diagonal product structures.
analysis.problem: Determine stability of smooth rank-one factors for higher-rank Anosov integer actions.
analysis.main_result: Assume the factor is a smooth fiber-bundle projection and some action element is the identity on the rank-one factor while Anosov on every fiber. Every sufficiently \(C^1\)-small smooth perturbation of the smooth action then retains a smooth rank-one factor. In particular, the diagonal product of two integer Anosov actions has \(C^1\)-stable product structure as an Anosov \(\mathbb Z^2\)-action.
analysis.context: Smooth factors and perturbations of higher-rank Anosov actions.

paper.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
paper.abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

analysis.relevance_note: Gibbs measures, symbolic horseshoes and homoclinic coding directly match thermodynamic and symbolic interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove existence and multiplicity results for homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees. They relate these measures to homoclinic orbits in finite-dimensional or Banach-space geometric settings.
analysis.problem: Study existence, superposition and dynamical representations of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures with integer spins.
analysis.main_result: A natural interaction summability assumption gives at least two measures satisfying two symmetry conditions. Two measures obeying a suitable nondegeneracy condition can be superimposed to produce infinitely many more. For bounded-support interactions, the measures correspond bijectively to suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of \(\mathbb R^{2n}\), with \(n\) the stated support bound. For \(n=1\), symbolic horseshoes give marginals concentrated near any finite subset of \(N\mathbb Z\) for sufficiently large \(N\). Infinite support leads instead to a Lagrangian correspondence on a Banach cotangent bundle. The summability, symmetry and nondegeneracy conditions are not detailed. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Tree Gibbs measures and homoclinic dynamics.

paper.title: The Intersection of nested filled-in little Julia sets have zero area
paper.abstract: It is shown that for any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial $Q_c$ the intersection $K_\infty$ of all the little filled-in Julia sets (renormalization Julia sets) containing the critical value have zero area.

analysis.relevance_note: Area of renormalization Julia-set intersections directly concerns fractal-set measure in complex dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For every infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial, the intersection of little filled-in Julia sets containing its critical value has zero area.
analysis.problem: Determine the area of the intersection of nested renormalization Julia sets.
analysis.main_result: The intersection of all little filled-in Julia sets containing the critical value of any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial has zero area. No further hypotheses or proof methods are stated. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Renormalization and area in quadratic complex dynamics.

paper.title: Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction in Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows
paper.abstract: The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow. Applied to contracting controlled skew-product semiflows, this gives exact descriptions of the chain recurrent set, chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins, and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge yields a complete Lyapunov function for the full semiflow while preserving the recurrent values of the base. The differential hypotheses are verified through subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms, allowing transient expansion and non-unique ergodicity. Quantitative persistence is established for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. The results provide a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor--repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics.

analysis.relevance_note: Chain recurrence, factors and attractor-repeller structure are central topological-dynamics themes.
analysis.tldr: The author reduces ambient chain attainability to a factor semiflow under an attracting-section and tracking hypothesis. Applications describe recurrent and invariant structures and construct a full Lyapunov function.
analysis.problem: Reduce chain relations of contracting controlled skew-product semiflows to their driving dynamics.
analysis.main_result: With an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking, chains can start off the section, but every attainable target lies on it and is determined by the factor semiflow. In contracting controlled skew products this describes chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge gives a complete Lyapunov function preserving base recurrent values. The differential checks permit transient expansion and nonunique ergodicity, and persistence is proved for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. Quantitative conditions are not given. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Topological recurrence and Lyapunov geometry of nonautonomous skew products.

paper.title: A structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems
paper.abstract: Recently, the author refuted several conjectures about the vanishing of multiple correlation sequences. The goal of this paper is to provide a counterpart for the conjectures of Frantzikinakis--Kuca and of Leibman. The significance of this manuscript is twofold: firstly, we provide a structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems along arithmetic progressions (in the sense of Frantzikinakis--Kuca), and a corresponding structure theorem for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds (in the sense of Leibman). Secondly, we identify null generalized nilsequences, as a notion of smallness, which provides a structured counterpart for null sequences. In particular, in the special case of ergodic nilsystems, we answer positively a question of Frantzikinakis on the structure of multiple correlation sequences.

analysis.relevance_note: Nilsequence structure and polynomial nilmanifold orbits give a substantial ergodic and homogeneous-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The author gives structure theorems for multiple correlations on nilsystems and polynomial subnilmanifold orbits. Null generalized nilsequences serve as a structured notion of smallness.
analysis.problem: Provide structured counterparts to failed vanishing conjectures for multiple correlations.
analysis.main_result: The paper treats correlations along arithmetic progressions and polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds, identifying null generalized nilsequences. In the ergodic nilsystem case it answers the cited question on multiple-correlation structure. The decompositions and their precise hypotheses are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Nilsystems, polynomial orbits and multiple correlations.

paper.title: Zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients
paper.abstract: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.

analysis.relevance_note: Melnikov distances and perturbed Hamiltonian chaos provide a smooth-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors estimate the average number of Melnikov-function zeros and the probability of no zeros for random-coefficient periodic perturbations. The asymptotics concern large and small perturbation periods.
analysis.problem: Quantify zeros of random Melnikov distance functions.
analysis.main_result: As the forcing period tends to large or small scales, the authors obtain asymptotic estimates for expected zero counts and zero-free probabilities. The coefficient distribution, formulas and additional assumptions are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Probabilistic analysis of Melnikov distance functions
analysis.context: Random periodic perturbations of Hamiltonian systems.

paper.title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
paper.abstract: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.

analysis.relevance_note: Weak mixing and recurrence along specified time sets directly connect measure-theoretic recurrence with topological and arithmetic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For any finite set of primes, the author constructs weakly mixing non-recurrence along the semigroup they generate. A broader criterion also covers an infinitely generated example.
analysis.problem: Determine recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of positive integers.
analysis.main_result: For every finite nonempty prime set \(\mathcal P\), there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving \(T\) and positive-measure \(A\) such that \(A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing\) for every \(r\in S_{\mathcal P}\). This answers the cited recurrence question negatively, including the times \(2^m3^n\). A sufficient criterion using divisibility and finitely many circle rotations also treats an infinitely generated semigroup outside every finite-prime semigroup. The general criterion is not explicitly formulated. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Divisibility properties and separation by finitely many circle rotations
analysis.context: Weak mixing and arithmetic recurrence sets.

paper.title: Magnetic billiards:duality and magnetic Radon property
paper.abstract: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2\pi/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant curves, periodic orbits and topological constructions give a substantial billiard-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The author constructs centrally symmetric magnetic billiard tables with invariant curves of four-periodic orbits. With the specified discrete rotational symmetry, the analogous periodic invariant curve forces circularity.
analysis.problem: Study magnetic Radon tables and rigidity of rotationally symmetric magnetic billiards.
analysis.main_result: For convex planar tables in a constant weak magnetic field, a functional family near circles has rotational invariant curves of four-periodic orbits with rotation number \(1/4\) or \(3/4\). Under rotational symmetry by \(2\pi/k\), a rotational invariant curve of \(k\)-periodic orbits exists exactly for circular tables. The paper also develops magnetic duality and standard and nonstandard generating functions for the outer magnetic billiard.
methods: Topological argument for the governing ODE system
analysis.context: Invariant structures and rigidity of magnetic billiards.

paper.title: Stationary Random Iterations of Lipschitz Maps: A Generalized Displacement Condition for the Existence of Invariant Structures
paper.abstract: We study random iterations generated by infinitely many Lipschitz maps on non-compact complete separable metric spaces. We generalize classical displacement conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of invariant structures. We prove two main results. The first uses the graph transform operator to extend Elton's condition [A multiplicative ergodic theorem for Lipschitz maps. Stochastic Process. Appl. 34(1) (1990)] for the existence and uniqueness of invariant graphs. The second uses the Markov operator to generalize a displacement condition for stationary measures, introduced by Diaconis and Freedman [Iterated random functions. SIAM Rev. 41(1) (1999)] and by Kloeckner [Optimal transportation and stationary measures for iterated function systems. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 173(1) (2022)]. We present several examples illustrating the applicability of our results.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant graphs and stationary measures for random iterations give an explicit invariant-measure connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors generalize displacement conditions for invariant structures of infinitely generated random Lipschitz iterations. Graph transforms handle invariant graphs and Markov operators handle stationary measures.
analysis.problem: Establish existence and uniqueness of invariant structures on noncompact complete separable metric spaces.
analysis.main_result: The graph-transform result extends Elton’s condition for existence and uniqueness of invariant graphs; a second result generalizes the cited stationary-measure displacement conditions using the Markov operator. Examples illustrate applicability. The generalized conditions and exact stationary-measure conclusions are not stated in detail. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Stationary random Lipschitz iterations.

paper.title: On tame amenable flows and generalized Newelski's conjecture
paper.abstract: We are developing some topological dynamics below a given ambit. We define and study Bohr compactifications below ambits and other related objects. We describe a natural epimorphism from the Ellis group of an ambit to the Bohr compactification below its Ellis semigroup ambit. The first main result says that, assuming tameness and hereditary amenability, this natural map is an isomorphism of topological groups. This is an abstract dynamical generalization of Newelski's conjecture, or rather a theorem of Chernikov and Simon that a natural map from the Ellis group of the flow $(S_G(M),G)$ to the definable Bohr compactification of $G$ is an isomorphism when $G$ is a definably amenable group definable in a NIP structure $M$. We give two proofs of our main result: a shorter dynamical proof and an analytic proof. In the course of the dynamical proof, we prove some results on the universal compactification flow and on the generalized Bohr compactification below a given ambit which admits a left continuous semigroup operation extending the action of $G$. The considerations around the analytic proof yield a description of the measured structure of amenable tame minimal flows, which is the second main result of this paper. We also study specializations of the above abstract topological dynamics context to model theory contexts to recover some known and to obtain some new notions and results. The main new results in the model theory contexts are: (i) a description of the Bohr compactification of the group of automorphisms of a sufficiently saturated model $\mathfrak{C}$ of a first order theory $T$ below a certain fundamental ambit associated with $\mathfrak{C}$; (ii) transfer of amenability of a NIP theory $T$ to amenability of the Ellis semigroup ambit; (iii) a version of Newelski's conjecture for spaces of local types with a description of Bohr compactifications below such spaces.

analysis.relevance_note: Tame amenable flows, Ellis groups and Bohr compactifications directly match topological group dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Under tameness and hereditary amenability, the natural Ellis-to-Bohr epimorphism is an isomorphism. The authors also describe measured structure of amenable tame minimal flows and obtain model-theoretic applications.
analysis.problem: Develop compactifications below ambits and relate their Ellis and Bohr groups.
analysis.main_result: For an ambit, the natural epimorphism from its Ellis group to the Bohr compactification below its Ellis semigroup ambit is a topological-group isomorphism under tameness and hereditary amenability. The paper also describes measured structure of amenable tame minimal flows, automorphism-group compactifications below a fundamental ambit, transfer of amenability of a NIP theory to its Ellis semigroup ambit, and a local-types version of Newelski’s conjecture. Detailed descriptions are not supplied. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Universal compactification and generalized Bohr compactification flows
analysis.context: Topological dynamics below ambits and model-theoretic compactifications.

paper.title: Thermodynamic formalism for partially hyperbolic endomorphisms with critical set
paper.abstract: We study the thermodynamic formalism of a broad class of partially hyperbolic, non-uniformly expanding endomorphisms with critical set, and show that they admit unique equilibrium states for all H\"older potentials of small variation. In particular, our results yield uniqueness of equilibrium states for Viana maps with small variation H\"older potentials, for non-uniformly expanding interval maps with finitely many critical points and hyperbolic H\"older potentials, and for Benedicks-Carleson quadratic maps with arbitrary H\"older potentials.

analysis.relevance_note: Equilibrium-state uniqueness is directly central to thermodynamic formalism.
analysis.tldr: The author proves uniqueness of equilibrium states for a class of partially hyperbolic nonuniformly expanding endomorphisms with critical sets. Applications include Viana, interval and Benedicks--Carleson quadratic maps with the stated potential restrictions.
analysis.problem: Obtain thermodynamic formalism in the presence of nonuniform expansion and critical points.
analysis.main_result: The general class has unique equilibrium states for Hölder potentials of small variation. The listed consequences are uniqueness for Viana maps with small-variation Hölder potentials, nonuniformly expanding interval maps with finitely many critical points and hyperbolic Hölder potentials, and Benedicks--Carleson quadratic maps with arbitrary Hölder potentials. The broad-class assumptions and variation threshold are not specified. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Thermodynamic formalism for nonuniformly expanding maps.

paper.title: Hausdorff and Packing Measures for $\beta$-L{\"u}roth Infinite Iterated Function Systems
paper.abstract: We study the Hausdorff and packing measures of attractors generated by infinite $\beta$-L\"uroth iterated function systems. Let $I\subset\mathbb N$ be infinite and let $\dim_H E_I=h$. For a regular system, we first give conditions for the positivity of $\mathcal H^h(E_I)$ and the finiteness of $\mathcal P^h(E_I)$ in terms of first-level L\"uroth intervals. We then introduce tail-regular partitions and the scale $R_n=\frac{B_n^\infty}{B_n}.$ Under tail-regularity, the Hausdorff and packing conditions reduce to counting conditions for $I$ on intervals of length comparable to $R_n$, together with a tail condition in the packing case. Finally, we apply these results to regularly varying partitions and stretched-exponential partitions.

analysis.relevance_note: Hausdorff and packing measures of infinite IFS attractors directly match fractal geometry.
analysis.tldr: The authors give positivity and finiteness criteria for critical-dimensional Hausdorff and packing measures of infinite beta-Lüroth attractors. Tail regularity reduces these to counting conditions and an additional packing-tail condition.
analysis.problem: Characterize critical-dimensional measures of infinite beta-Lüroth iterated function systems.
analysis.main_result: For a regular system with infinite digit set \(I\) and \(\dim_H E_I=h\), first-level Lüroth intervals give conditions for positivity of \(\mathcal H^h(E_I)\) and finiteness of \(\mathcal P^h(E_I)\). Under tail regularity, these become counts on intervals comparable to \(R_n=B_n^\infty/B_n\), together with a packing-tail condition. Applications concern regularly varying and stretched-exponential partitions. The conditions and scale components are not defined explicitly. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Tail-regular partitions and scale-dependent counting conditions
analysis.context: Measures of infinite-system fractal attractors.

paper.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions II: quadratic differential equations
paper.abstract: We investigate differential equations defined through elements of a nonassociative five-dimensional real algebra $\mathcal A_\gamma$, and show that every system of quadratic differential equations $\dot p=F(p)$ on $\mathbb R^5$ can be written as a differential equation over such a non-flexible quadratic algebra. We then study quadratic differential equations and their solutions over the whole family $\{\mathcal A_\gamma\}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}$ of algebras while varying $\gamma$ across the parameter interval $[0,1]$, exploiting the fact that by definition, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra and that $\mathcal A_1=\mathbb{P}$ is the real Pentarnion algebra. We construct explicit Jacobi elliptic solutions that deform a quaternion-valued solution at $\gamma=0$ into a Pentarnion-valued one at $\gamma=1$, and an algebra-valued Riccati equation whose equilibrium $p=0$ loses stability at a critical value of $\gamma$. Numerical experiments indicate period doubling, coexisting stable periodic orbits and irregular dynamics.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is algebra-valued quadratic ODEs and numerical bifurcations, without a central entropy, fractal or symbolic theme.

paper.title: A Five-Dimensional Nonassociative Algebra: elliptic integrability and bracketing-dependent dynamics
paper.abstract: We introduce a five-dimensional nonassociative real algebra $\mathbb{P}$ whose one-generated subalgebras are complex while its left, middle, and right nuclei are all $\mathbb{R}$. This contrast permits an unambiguous one-element functional calculus but makes polynomial ordinary differential equations sensitive to bracketing. We classify the homogeneous quadratic words containing one fixed coefficient $B$ and two copies of $p$ that preserve $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{1,B,p\}$. For a fixed-coefficient family of Pentarnion ODEs interpolating between $B(pp)$ and $(Bp)p$, changing only the bracketing preserves the linearisation but changes the observed global dynamics. Exact balance identities isolate the associator contribution, while numerical diagnostics support bounded chaos at one endpoint and an attracting periodic orbit at the other. The flexibility defect $p(Bp)-(pB)p=-[p,B,p]$ also produces a rank jump: after polarisation, one-generated subalgebras have dimension three on a nonempty Zariski-open set, rather than at most two. On a canonical invariant three-dimensional space the resulting flow has two first integrals and an explicit periodic orbit on an elliptic curve. We also construct a dense five-dimensional quadratic flow with a full-affine-span Jacobi-elliptic solution. Its projective closure is an elliptic normal sextic, and representation by two ordered products selects the modulus $m=1/2$.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is nonassociative algebra and explicitly integrable or numerically studied ODEs, without a central profile theme.

paper.title: Finiteness of ergodic measures of maximal entropy for certain skew product systems
paper.abstract: Consider a $C^{1+\beta}$ skew product $F$ over a topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphism $f$, with fiber dynamics driven by a $C^{1+\beta}$ $\mathbb{R}^k$-action $\{\rho_{\bf t}\}$ on a closed manifold $Y$ through a $C^{1+\beta}$ cocycle $\tau$. Suppose that the fiber action preserves an ergodic smooth measure of maximal entropy $m_{\operatorname{MME}}$. Under a nondegeneracy condition called joint nontriviality, and assuming that each element $\rho_{\bf t}$ is either of class $C^\infty$ or hyperbolic, we prove that $F$ admits only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy. Moreover, every such measure is of the form $\mu\times m_{\operatorname{MME}}$, where $\mu$ is an ergodic equilibrium state for a H\"older potential on the base. If, in addition, the fiber action is exponentially mixing of all orders, then every ergodic MME is Bernoulli, exponentially mixing of all orders, and satisfies the Central Limit Theorem. Our main novelties are entropy formulas for skew products, obtained through the cone property and $r$-neutralized entropy, and a relative Ledrappier--Young theorem that converts the fiber entropy contribution into absolute continuity of fiberwise conditional measures. Combined with nonlinear thermodynamic formalism, rotation theory and Yomdin theory, these yield the finiteness of the base projections and the product rigidity of ergodic MMEs.

analysis.relevance_note: Maximal-entropy measures, equilibrium states, group actions and entropy formulas are central to the profile.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove finiteness and product rigidity of ergodic maximal-entropy measures for specified Anosov-base skew products. Additional higher-order exponential mixing of the fiber action gives Bernoulli, mixing and central-limit conclusions.
analysis.problem: Classify ergodic maximal-entropy measures of skew products driven by a smooth real group action.
analysis.main_result: Consider a \(C^{1+\beta}\) skew product over a topologically mixing Anosov map, driven through a \(C^{1+\beta}\) cocycle by an \(\mathbb R^k\)-action on a closed fiber. Assume the action preserves an ergodic smooth MME, joint nontriviality, and every action element is smooth or hyperbolic. There are finitely many ergodic MMEs, all products of that fiber measure and base ergodic Hölder equilibrium states. If the action is exponentially mixing of all orders, each product MME is Bernoulli, exponentially mixing of all orders and satisfies a CLT. Joint nontriviality is not defined. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Entropy and product rigidity in smooth skew products.

paper.title: Quasicircularity of the Zakeri Curve and Capture Component Boundaries
paper.abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number of bounded type, we prove that the locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the boundary of the fixed Siegel disk is a quasicircle. This locus is known as the Zakeri curve. The main step is a boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic families of disks with uniformly quasiconformal extensions. We further prove that every capture component in this family is a quasidisk, including components attached to the Zakeri curve.

analysis.relevance_note: Quasicircle and quasidisk geometry of polynomial parameter loci gives a clear complex-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: For a fixed bounded-type irrational rotation number, the authors prove the Zakeri curve is a quasicircle. Every capture component in the family is also a quasidisk, including attached components.
analysis.problem: Determine quasiconformal geometry of the Zakeri locus and capture-component boundaries.
analysis.main_result: The locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the fixed Siegel-disk boundary is a quasicircle when the fixed irrational rotation number has bounded type. All capture components in this family are quasidisks, including those attached to this curve.
methods: Boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic disk families with uniformly quasiconformal extensions
analysis.context: Parameter geometry of cubic Siegel dynamics.

paper.title: Bistable fronts in periodic media: phase reduction and realization of circle flows
paper.abstract: We establish a phase reduction and a converse realization theorem for front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations. For sufficiently large periods under local bistability, and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation admits a stationary front, we construct strictly ordered invariant front families that are normally exponentially attracting and locally complete for entire orbits. Modulo spatial-period translations, the dynamics on each family reduces exactly to a circle flow: rotations correspond to propagating pulsating fronts, equilibria to stationary fronts, and connecting orbits to transition fronts between stationary fronts. Conversely, every smooth circle flow can be realized, up to time-preserving topological conjugacy, as the quotient dynamics of such a family for a periodic, locally bistable equation with constant diffusion and no advection. Realizations with a Cantor set of stationary phases and a connecting orbit in each complementary interval illustrate the richness of front dynamics in these media. We also obtain first-order phase-velocity expansions in both period limits, quantitative propagation laws near zero frozen speed, and global exponential orbital stability of propagating pulsating fronts.

analysis.relevance_note: Exact topological realization of circle flows, including Cantor stationary sets, makes topological dynamics central despite the PDE setting.
analysis.tldr: The authors reduce ordered attracting front families exactly to circle flows and conversely realize every smooth circle flow by a periodic bistable equation. Rotations, equilibria and connecting orbits encode propagating, stationary and transition fronts.
analysis.problem: Reduce and realize front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations.
analysis.main_result: Strictly ordered normally exponentially attracting front families are constructed for sufficiently large periods under local bistability and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation has a stationary front. They are locally complete for entire orbits; quotienting spatial-period translations gives exact circle flows. Conversely, every smooth circle flow is realized up to time-preserving topological conjugacy by a periodic locally bistable equation with constant diffusion and no advection. Cantor stationary-phase examples, first-order phase velocities, quantitative propagation laws and global exponential orbital stability of propagating fronts are also obtained. Quantitative thresholds are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Topological realization of circle dynamics through bistable fronts.

paper.title: Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
paper.abstract: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.

analysis.relevance_note: Mixed-radix odometers and temporal statistics directly connect symbolic topological systems with ergodic theory.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove a temporal CLT for visits of a mixed-radix odometer near the origin, with random orbit length and interval endpoint. The theorem includes a Kolmogorov--Smirnov convergence rate under two stated types of conditions.
analysis.problem: Describe fluctuations of odometer visit discrepancy under independently uniform choices of time length and interval endpoint.
analysis.main_result: A Feller-type condition and an explicit condition approximating the finite random-time clock by a Haar clock at fluctuation scale yield a temporal CLT with an explicit Kolmogorov--Smirnov rate. This extends the cited fixed-base theorem to mixed radices. The conditions and rate formula are not given. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Approximation of a finite random-time clock by a Haar clock
analysis.context: Temporal discrepancy statistics in odometer dynamics.

paper.title: Network of limit sets in dynamical systems
paper.abstract: Points within a topological dynamical systems can be separated into transient and recurrent points. Most of the asymptotic properties of the dynamics is borne by the closure of the collection of recurrent points. This article presents a representation scheme for dynamics using the connectivity information in terms of the recurrent set. This representation is functorial and represents certain compositional features of dynamical systems.

analysis.relevance_note: Recurrent-set representation and functorial composition are explicitly topological-dynamics themes.
analysis.tldr: The author proposes a functorial representation of dynamics using recurrent-set connectivity. It records certain compositional features of systems.
analysis.problem: Represent topological dynamical systems through connectivity information involving recurrent points.
analysis.main_result: The representation is functorial and captures certain compositional features. The representation’s precise definition, hypotheses and encoded composition rules are not specified. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Recurrent and transient structure in topological dynamics.

paper.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems along oscillating sequences
paper.abstract: We establish the first pointwise convergence result for nonconventional ergodic averages modeled along a large class of oscillating sequences, treating, for example, orbits of the form $\big(\lfloor n^d\sin(e\pi n)\rfloor\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$. More specifically, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ equipped with an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T\colon X\to X$ and every $f\in L^p_{\mu}(X)$ with $p\in(1,\infty]$, we prove that the limit \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf\big(T^{\lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor}x\big)\quad\text{exists for $\mu$-a.e. $x\in X$,} \] where $P$ is a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients, $\psi$ is $1$-periodic and real-analytic, and $\alpha$ has irrationality exponent smaller than $1+\sqrt{\operatorname{deg}(P)+1}$. On the one hand, the latter assumption is satisfied by a.e. $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, and, on the other hand, our result covers any of the following concrete orbits \[ \lfloor n\cos(e\pi n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\lfloor n^{37}\sin(n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\big\lfloor \sqrt{2}n^{10}e^{\sin(\pi (\sqrt[5]{7}+1) n)}\big\rfloor\text{,}\quad \big\lfloor \big((\log 2) n^3+e n\big)e^{e^{\cos(\pi \sqrt{2} n)}}\big\rfloor\text{.} \] The proof employs the so-called one-frequency circle method for estimating exponential sums with phases $\big(\xi \lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor\big)_{1\le n\le N}$, but the major arc approximants of our exponential sums do not consist of their direct continuous counterparts. In the major arc regime we decouple the $\psi$-oscillatory part of the phase from the polynomial one, and approximate the exponential sum by $\int_0^1\big(\frac{1}{N}\int_0^Ne^{2\pi i\xi P(t)\psi( s)}dt\big)ds$. This represents a novel phenomenon for problems of this kind, and, interestingly, our proof exploits the coefficient-free variational estimates of Radon-type operators.

analysis.relevance_note: Pointwise averages and oscillatory return times provide a substantial ergodic-theory connection.
analysis.tldr: The author proves almost-everywhere convergence of ergodic averages sampled by polynomially scaled analytic oscillations. The frequency is restricted by an irrationality-exponent bound, and the proof uses exponential-sum and variational estimates.
analysis.problem: Establish pointwise convergence along oscillating integer sequences.
analysis.main_result: For invertible probability-preserving \(T\), \(f\in L^p\) with \(1<p\leq\infty\), nonconstant real polynomial \(P\), and real-analytic one-periodic \(\psi\), averages of \(f(T^{\lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor}x)\) converge almost everywhere if the irrationality exponent of \(\alpha\) is smaller than \(1+\sqrt{\deg(P)+1}\). This condition holds for almost every real frequency. The proof’s major-arc approximation separates polynomial and oscillatory parts rather than directly replacing the sum by its continuous counterpart.
methods: Coefficient-free variational estimates for Radon-type operators
analysis.context: Pointwise ergodic theory along oscillating sequences.

paper.title: Constellations for Lyapunov exponents
paper.abstract: We study the maximal Lyapunov exponent of random products of positive matrices, and prove that it can be calculated to arbitrary precision with arithmetic work polynomial in the number of requested digits. In nondegenerate settings, the complexity of our method depends on the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics---which we characterize---and not on the Euclidean dimension of the ambient space in which the dynamics live. As numerical applications, we determine the Hausdorff dimension of random intersections of Sierpi\'nski gaskets, and Viswanath's constant---the growth rate of the random Fibonacci sequence. We first establish a general inequality for nonnegative matrix families showing that, if a signed measure with finite support is sufficiently close to being stationary, then it predicts the Lyapunov exponent accurately. This framework also encompasses Pollicott's Fredholm determinant approximation. We then show that, just like drawing a constellation by picking bright stars, one can construct a sequence of signed measures approximating stationarity by picking informative orbits of the projective dynamics. Furthermore, we prove that our construction uses an asymptotically optimal number of atoms, which is governed by an intrinsic quantity we call constellation dimension.

analysis.relevance_note: Intrinsic approximation dimension and Hausdorff-dimension applications connect the Lyapunov computation directly to dimension theory.
analysis.tldr: The author computes maximal Lyapunov exponents of random positive-matrix products with arithmetic work polynomial in requested digits. Approximate stationary signed measures yield an asymptotically optimal orbit-based construction governed by constellation dimension.
analysis.problem: Approximate maximal random-matrix Lyapunov exponents efficiently using intrinsic projective dynamics.
analysis.main_result: A finitely supported signed measure close enough to stationarity accurately predicts the exponent for nonnegative matrix families. Informative projective orbits produce such measures with an asymptotically optimal number of atoms governed by constellation dimension. For positive matrices the arithmetic work is polynomial in requested digits; in nondegenerate settings its complexity depends on characterized intrinsic dynamics rather than ambient Euclidean dimension. Numerical applications determine random Sierpiński-intersection Hausdorff dimension and Viswanath’s constant. Exact complexity and stationarity bounds are not supplied. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Lyapunov computation, projective dynamics and intrinsic dimension.

paper.title: Variational principle for the Carath\'eodory--Pesin entropy of foliations
paper.abstract: We introduce Carath\'eodory-Pesin structures for non-singular foliations on Riemannian manifolds and define a new notion of entropy for such foliations. Under dynamical and geometric assumptions on the corresponding holonomy pseudogroups, we establish a variational description of this new concept which relates it to the local metric entropy of measures on transversals and to the entropy of harmonic measures on the manifold.

analysis.relevance_note: A new foliation entropy and variational description directly match entropy and variational-principle interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors define Carathéodory--Pesin entropy for nonsingular foliations. Under holonomy assumptions it admits a variational description involving transversal local entropy and harmonic-measure entropy.
analysis.problem: Define foliation entropy and relate it variationally to measure entropies.
analysis.main_result: Carathéodory--Pesin structures on nonsingular foliations of Riemannian manifolds produce a new entropy. Under dynamical and geometric hypotheses on holonomy pseudogroups, its variational description relates local metric entropy on transversals to entropy of harmonic measures on the manifold. The assumptions and formula are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Entropy theory of foliations.

paper.title: Quantitative Persistence and Regularity of Invariant Graphs for Dissipative Twist Maps
paper.abstract: In this paper we study the robustness of invariant Lagrangian graphs for dissipative twist maps on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$ in the $C^r$ category, for any $r\ge 1$, and show their persistence as invariant global attractors under quantitative sharp conditions involving both the size of dissipation parameter and the perturbation at stake. Note that when $d>1$ the geometric Lagrangian property of the invariant manifold may be destroyed, so that the graph may persist but fail to be Lagrangian. In general, additional dynamical requirements on the twist maps come into play if we intend to preserve also the Lagrangian property. In this line, we first study their persistence for general perturbations, then we restrict to the class of exact conformally symplectic twist maps and provide quantitative sharp conditions for the persistence of invariant exact Lagrangian graphs, without assuming any condition on the tangential dynamics of the manifold. The persistence result relies on a combination of a suitable multidimensional Herman--Mather formula proved in this setting and contraction estimates that provide sharp bounds on the $C^1$-norm of the perturbation to get a unique, globally attracting $C^r$ graph. In dimension $d=1$, by further assuming that that the circle map induced by the graph has irrational rotation number, we prove that every $C^1$ invariant graph of a $C^k$ map is $C^k$ for $k=2,3,\ldots,\infty$. Analytic maps with Lipschitz, non-$C^1$ invariant graphs at every prescribed irrational rotation number show that this initial regularity assumption is essential.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant graphs, global attraction and irrational circle dynamics give a substantial smooth-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove sharp quantitative persistence of attracting graphs for dissipative twist maps and explain when the Lagrangian property persists. In one dimension, initial continuously differentiable graph regularity upgrades under irrational rotation.
analysis.problem: Control persistence and regularity of invariant graphs under dissipative twist-map perturbations.
analysis.main_result: For \(C^r\) maps, \(r\geq1\), quantitative dissipation and perturbation bounds give a unique globally attracting \(C^r\) graph. In dimensions above one it may cease to be Lagrangian; exact conformally symplectic maps have separate sharp conditions preserving exact Lagrangian graphs, without tangential-dynamics assumptions. In dimension one, an irrational induced rotation number upgrades a \(C^1\) invariant graph of a \(C^k\) map to \(C^k\), including the smooth case. Analytic examples with Lipschitz non-\(C^1\) graphs show the initial regularity is essential. Exact bounds are not given. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Dissipative twist maps and invariant Lagrangian graphs.

paper.title: Large deviations for observables with logarithmic singularity and differentiability of the pressure function
paper.abstract: We show that logarithmic observables of form $\phi(x)=\log(|x-b|)$ on the doubling map $T$ have exponential large deviations with respect to the invariant measure if $b$ is preperiodic but not periodic with respect to $T$ giving a counterpart to the known result of strictly stretched exponential large deviations in the case that $b$ is periodic. These results are established by showing that the topological pressure function developed for unbounded observables is differentiable at $0$.

analysis.relevance_note: Pressure differentiability and large deviations for unbounded potentials are central thermodynamic themes.
analysis.tldr: For logarithmic singularities at preperiodic nonperiodic points of the doubling map, the authors prove exponential large deviations. They establish this through differentiability of the unbounded-observable pressure at zero.
analysis.problem: Determine large-deviation behavior of logarithmic observables depending on the singular point’s orbit.
analysis.main_result: For the doubling map and \(\phi(x)=\log|x-b|\), a preperiodic but nonperiodic \(b\) gives exponential large deviations with respect to the invariant measure. This contrasts with the cited strictly stretched-exponential periodic-point case. The pressure function is differentiable at zero; the invariant measure and quantitative bounds are not identified more precisely. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Differentiability at zero of topological pressure for unbounded observables
analysis.context: Pressure and deviations for singular observables.

paper.title: A non-perturbative topological persistence theorem for normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds
paper.abstract: Floer proved that, under a sufficiently small $C^0$ perturbation, a normally hyperbolic invariant manifold gives rise to a nearby invariant set whose cohomology ring contains a subring isomorphic to that of the original manifold. Using topological conditions, expressed in terms of the so-called covering relations, we generalize this theorem to a non-perturbative context. Our result does not require the existence of an invariant manifold before perturbation, nor does it require the original map to be smooth or invertible. For the proof, we develop an additional structure on the Conley index for maps on vector bundles.

analysis.relevance_note: Topological persistence and cohomological invariant-set information directly connect topology and dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors extend a cohomological persistence theorem to a nonperturbative setting using covering relations. No pre-existing invariant manifold, smoothness or invertibility is required.
analysis.problem: Generalize the invariant-set cohomology conclusion associated with normally hyperbolic persistence.
analysis.main_result: Covering-relation conditions yield a nonperturbative extension of Floer’s theorem in which a nearby invariant set contains, in its cohomology ring, a copy of the original manifold’s cohomology ring. The new context does not require an invariant manifold before perturbation or a smooth or invertible original map. The covering conditions and precise cohomological construction are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Additional Conley-index structure for maps on vector bundles
analysis.context: Topological persistence of invariant sets.

paper.title: Influence of Anthropisation on a Mosquito Community in a Tropical Forest-Village Interface
paper.abstract: Tropical forests are undergoing deep changes caused by human activities, which have repercussions on the habitats of wild animal, particularly mammals. As mammals serve as a main source of blood meals for forest mosquitoes, their decline may affect the mosquitoes, as do changes in their habitats and abiotic conditions, such as rainfall, temperature, etc. Finally, along with humans come new species of mosquitoes-more generalist and more anthropophilic-that adapt to these new conditions and, moreover, serve as vectors for re-emerging diseases against which local populations have no more immunity. In this work, we derive a deterministic model which includes the effects of anthropisation, two species of mosquito that interact with one another (one is a generalist, whilst the other is sedentary and lives in the forest), and blood feeding preferences between multiple blood sources. We consider two socio-ecological areas, corresponding to a domestic area (for instance, a village), and a wild area (for instance, a tropical forest). A comprehensive analysis of the system is carried out using classical theory and monotone systems theory. We analyse the efficiency of individual protective measures, such as mosquito nets and repellents, against the domestic mosquito species. We investigate the risk of invasion of the wild area by a generalist mosquito species. We show that habitat anthropisation and high interspecific competition facilitate the invasion. When the mathematical system converges towards a periodic cycle, we provide numerical estimates for the periodic invasion threshold. Using a global sensitivity analysis, we show that the model is sensitive to the level of anthropisation, the adaptability of the invasive species to the forest area, and its fitness. The more efficient way to control the invasion is, therefore, to limit, as much as possible, the forest anthropisation.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is mosquito ecology, invasion modeling and intervention analysis, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: The Formal Critical Coupling of the Four-Dimensional Anderson Model
paper.abstract: In this work we present a formal renormalization-group (RG) calculation for the weakly coupled four-dimensional elliptic Anderson model. Under a scale-independent bare-coupling convention, and with the normalization $\lambda_{\varepsilon}$, the bubble-chain resummation yields the geometric series $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$, with a formal pole at $\lambda_c$. We stress that this pole is a feature of the formal bare bubble series. The argument combines Bogoliubov-Parasiuk-Hepp-Zimmermann (BPHZ) renormalization, a Hepp-sector motivated restriction to the bubble-chain subclass for explicit resummation, and an explicit summation of the resulting geometric series. Numerically, we illustrate the analytic building blocks of the formal expansion: the massive Green function, the bubble integral, the geometric resummation, the extraction of the formal pole from synthetic noisy data, a kurtosis diagnostic, and a phase diagram of the formal variance. These computations visualize the deterministic kernels and the formal resummation used above. Using spectral methods and nonlinear least-squares fitting, we verify the short-distance asymptotic behaviour of the massive Green function for $G=(1-\Delta)^{-1}\delta_0$, reproduce the logarithmic divergence of the bubble integral in four dimensions, compute the formal effective variance $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$ arising from the bubble-chain resummation, locate the formal pole at $\lambda_c$, and draw a schematic phase diagram of the formal variance in the $(\lambda,\log\varepsilon)$ plane. The kurtosis diagnostic uses a synthetic proxy for the non-Gaussian regime; the sharp change is imposed by construction. Nonlinear fitting of synthetic data recovers the formal pole within the statistical uncertainty of the synthetic noise. Our results illustrate the analytic formulas and the fitting procedure.

analysis.relevance_note: This is a formal physical-model renormalization calculation with synthetic numerical illustrations, without a central profile theme.

paper.title: Periodic data conjugacy for diffeomorphism cocycles
paper.abstract: We consider H\"older continuous cocycles over a hyperbolic dynamical system with values in the group of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold. We focus on establishing conjugacy between two cocycles from conjugacy of their periodic data. We obtain such a result under bunching, or domination, assumption on the cocycles and a mild regularity assumption in $C^0$ topology on the maps conjugating the periodic data. We also obtain conjugacy to a constant cocycle assuming boundedness in $C^1$ or pre-compactness in $C^0$ for the constant cocycle and the conjugating maps.

analysis.relevance_note: Cocycle conjugacy, periodic data and hyperbolic dynamics provide a clear rigidity-related connection.
analysis.tldr: The author derives conjugacy of diffeomorphism-valued cocycles from conjugate periodic data under bunching and regularity conditions. Additional boundedness or precompactness assumptions give conjugacy to a constant.
analysis.problem: Recover global cocycle conjugacy from periodic-data conjugacy.
analysis.main_result: For Hölder cocycles over a hyperbolic system with values in diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold, bunching or domination and mild \(C^0\)-regularity of periodic conjugators yield conjugacy. A constant-cocycle result assumes \(C^1\)-boundedness or \(C^0\)-precompactness of the constant cocycle and conjugating maps. The detailed bunching and regularity requirements are not given. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Periodic-data rigidity of diffeomorphism cocycles.

paper.title: Graph-Convolutional Reinforcement Learning for Finite-Time Stabilization of a Chaotic Chua Circuit via Unified Flexible Terminal Sliding-Mode Control
paper.abstract: This paper introduces a graph convolutional reinforcement learning framework for the finite-time stabilization of chaotic dynamics in a physical Chua circuit. The circuit is modeled directly in terms of capacitor voltages, inductor current, and physical component parameters. This preserves the connection between the mathematical model and the underlying electrical system. A unified, flexible terminal sliding-mode controller is developed to achieve stabilization within a finite time in the presence of uncertainties in the lumped model, external disturbances, and bounded control inputs. The controller incorporates state-dependent nonlinear exponents to provide flexible convergence characteristics while avoiding singular terms near equilibrium. To minimize dependence on manual controller tuning, the admissible controller parameters are optimized using an actor-critic reinforcement learning scheme with a graph convolutional network that leverages the circuit dynamics' coupling structure. The learned parameters are constrained to the ranges required by the theoretical stability conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the rapid suppression of chaotic oscillations and the finite-time convergence of the state and sliding variables while respecting the prescribed input-saturation limits. Compared to a reference control method, the proposed approach reduces the IAE, ISE, ITAE, and ITSE by 56.27\,\%, 56.40\,\%, 61.69\,\%, and 64.70\,\%, respectively. These results suggest that graph-based reinforcement learning can effectively tune parameters while retaining the robustness and analytical structure of the underlying sliding-mode controller.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is circuit stabilization and reinforcement-learning controller tuning rather than the central entropy, dimension or symbolic themes.

paper.title: Local Koopman modes of saddle-point diffusions: exact singular functions and a data-driven estimator
paper.abstract: Coherent sets-regions of phase space that resist mixing-organize transport in stochastic dynamical systems and are encoded in the leading singular functions of the stochastic Koopman operator. These are typically computed numerically and globally; a local, analytic theory near a fixed point has been missing, although fixed points and the transitions between them organize the flow. We supply the local theory for a saddle, the transition state through which probability flows between basins. Naively the construction fails-probability escapes along unstable directions, the invariant measure is non-normalizable, the singular functions leave $L^2$, and singular values exceed one. We show that conditioning on non-escape (a Doob's $h$-transform) repairs this; that the required $h$ is the unique stabilizing solution of an algebraic Riccati equation; and that the resulting slow modes decay at the escape rate along the unstable manifold. We obtain these modes in closed form-products of Hermite polynomials in canonical coordinates times the $h$-function-and use their unitary structure to derive a data-driven estimator: canonical correlation analysis on conditioned trajectories. When a single unstable direction dominates, the leading mode is the reaction coordinate, locally recovering the stable manifold and committor of transition-path theory. The construction connects coherent sets to transition-path theory, to the stabilizing Riccati solution of linear control, and to the time-reversed dynamics of generative diffusion models.

analysis.relevance_note: Koopman modes, coherent sets and conditioned invariant structures give a substantial operator-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The author obtains local singular functions near a stochastic saddle after conditioning on nonescape. Closed-form modes yield a conditioned-trajectory estimator and, under a dominant unstable direction, a local reaction coordinate.
analysis.problem: Develop an analytic local Koopman singular-function theory at a saddle where unconditioned probability escapes.
analysis.main_result: A Doob \(h\)-transform repairs nonnormalizability and singular-function problems; \(h\) is given by the unique stabilizing algebraic Riccati solution. Slow modes decay at the unstable-manifold escape rate and are Hermite-polynomial products times \(h\) in canonical coordinates. Unitary structure gives a canonical-correlation estimator on conditioned trajectories. If one unstable direction dominates, the leading mode locally recovers the stable manifold and committor. The precise diffusion assumptions are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Stochastic Koopman analysis and transition-path geometry.

paper.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
paper.abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.

analysis.relevance_note: Recovering the group and its topological action from an algebra directly matches group-action classification.
analysis.tldr: The authors classify isometric isomorphisms of summable crossed products. These Banach algebras remember the compact space, discrete group and action up to topological isomorphism.
analysis.problem: Determine which dynamical information is recovered by an isometric crossed-product Banach algebra.
analysis.main_result: For actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces, the \(\ell^1\)-crossed products are isometrically isomorphic exactly when the actions are topologically isomorphic. Thus the algebra is not determined by the transformation groupoid alone. Analogous measurable-action results are also obtained; their precise formulation is not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Recovery of continuous functions from hermitian elements
Geometry of Lebesgue spaces to identify invertible isometries
analysis.context: Banach crossed products and dynamical reconstruction.

paper.title: Locally eventually onto cellular automata
paper.abstract: We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is locally eventually onto. The appendix provides the algorithms that check these finite criteria and then presents examples of locally eventually onto, non-bipermutive cellular automata for small diameters.

analysis.relevance_note: Cellular automata, cylinder images and local eventual surjectivity directly match symbolic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors provide finite criteria for one-dimensional cellular automata to be locally eventually onto. Block-regularity generalizes bipermutivity and, with two further conditions, forces eventual full images of every cylinder.
analysis.problem: Decide openness and local eventual surjectivity of finite-alphabet cellular automata.
analysis.main_result: In the stated setting, openness is equivalent to a fixed finite-to-one multiplicity and implies surjectivity. A de Bruijn-graph method decides openness and its multiplicity. Block-regularity implies openness; together with two extra conditions it makes every nonempty cylinder eventually map onto the whole configuration space. Algorithms and small-diameter non-bipermutive examples are supplied. The finite criteria are not explicitly stated. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Openness and local eventual surjectivity in symbolic cellular dynamics.

paper.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
paper.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n$ if $\lambda_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $\lambda_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.

analysis.relevance_note: Height growth under rational iteration gives an arithmetic orbit-growth connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors give uniform height-growth bounds in terms of the first dynamical degree and variety dimension. The arguments distinguish number fields from curve function fields.
analysis.problem: Control heights along well-defined forward orbits of dominant rational self-maps.
analysis.main_result: Let the normal projective variety have dimension \(d\), and choose ample height \(h_H\geq1\). Uniformly in \(n\geq1\) and points with defined forward orbit, heights are at most \(C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n\) when \(\lambda_1(f)>1\), and \(C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}\) when \(\lambda_1(f)=1\). The base field is a number field or the function field of a curve.
methods: Uniform arithmetic-degree bound and height comparison over number fields
Uniform geometric-degree bound on a projective model over function fields
analysis.context: Arithmetic dynamics of rational self-maps.

paper.title: Improved Global Boundedness Criteria via Refined Bootstrap Estimates for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis-May-Nowak System
paper.abstract: We study a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system with nonlinear diffusion growing at least as $s^{m-1}$ at high densities and derive improved criteria for global existence and uniform boundedness. For the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic system, we establish global boundedness when $m>3-\frac{4}{n}$ for $n\in\{2,3\}$ and when $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. For the fully parabolic system, the same conclusion holds under $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. The proof relies on two refined estimates. Weighted space--time control of the nonlinear infection source yields the low-order $L^q$-bounds for the free virus density needed to initiate the bootstrap in the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic case. Subsequently, preserving the product structure of this source in the interpolation argument allows the chemotactic contribution to be absorbed more efficiently by the nonlinear diffusion. These estimates improve the previously known sufficient conditions for global boundedness.

analysis.relevance_note: This concerns PDE boundedness criteria for a chemotaxis infection model, without central entropy, fractal or topological-dynamics content.

paper.title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
paper.abstract: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is not homeomorphic to a line and, provided that it has codimension at least $2$, cannot have a single end at infinity.

analysis.relevance_note: Topological connectedness and global invertibility give an indirect qualitative-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Connected preimages of large circles imply planar polynomial global invertibility when the Jacobian never vanishes. Higher-dimensional counterexamples and three-dimensional restrictions show the limitation of this criterion.
analysis.problem: Relate connected sphere preimages to global polynomial invertibility.
analysis.main_result: A polynomial map of \(\mathbb R^2\) with nowhere-zero Jacobian is a global diffeomorphism if preimages of large circles are connected. This implication fails in higher dimensions. In dimension three, connected large-sphere preimages imply its Jelonek set is not homeomorphic to a line; with codimension at least two, it cannot have a single end at infinity.
methods: Counterexample families in higher dimensions; further proof methods are not stated
analysis.context: Polynomial invertibility and topology at infinity.

paper.title: The measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups
paper.abstract:
In this article we show that all the nonamenable Baumslag-Solitar groups with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree, i.e., $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ with $|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p|
eq |q|$, are measure equivalent to each other, thereby completing the measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups: each $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ belongs to one of three measure equivalence classes according to whether it is amenable ($|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$), virtually isomorphic to $\mathbf{F}_n 	imes \mathbf{Z}$ ($|p|=|q|
eq 1$), or is nonamenable with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree ($|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p| 
eq |q|$). More generally, we obtain the similar classification of the generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups of rank $1$ (i.e., groups that act cocompactly on a tree with edge and vertex stabilizers infinite cyclic). Our proof also establishes a classification of all treeable lcsc groups into exactly six measure equivalence classes. Our new contribution which completes this taxonomy is: all nonunimodular nonamenable treeable lcsc groups are measure equivalent. Along the way we obtain several results about type $\mathrm{III}$ equivalence relations and graphings of independent interest. For example, we show that every ergodic type $\mathrm{III}_0$ graphing admits an ergodic hyperfinite subgraph for which the natural factor map of Krieger flows is an isomorphism.

analysis.relevance_note: Measure equivalence, amenability and treeable group actions directly match the group-dynamics profile.
analysis.tldr: The authors complete the measure-equivalence classification of Baumslag--Solitar groups into three classes. Their proof also completes a six-class taxonomy for treeable locally compact second countable groups.

The three Baumslag--Solitar classes are the amenable case \(|p|=1\) or \(|q|=1\), the virtually free-group-times-integers case \(|p|=|q|

All nonunimodular nonamenable treeable locally compact second countable groups are measure equivalent, completing six classes. Every ergodic type-\(\mathrm{III}_0\) graphing also has an ergodic hyperfinite subgraph inducing an isomorphism of Krieger flows. The full six-class list is not given. Not specified in the abstract.
