analysis.context: Measure equivalence and treeability of groups.

paper.title: Extrapolating learned dynamics across bifurcations based on generalized synchronization
paper.abstract: Predicting dynamics across bifurcations by extrapolating trained models is crucial in diverse fields of physics. Generalized synchronization provides a framework for understanding dynamical reconstruction by neural networks, especially in the context of reservoir computing. Building on this framework, we derive a formula combining pretrained readouts to reconstruct unseen chaotic dynamics. Using classical Lagrange interpolation theory, we derive rigorous bounds on readout errors and conjugacy residuals. Numerical examples demonstrate accurate prediction of chaotic dynamics across bifurcations.

analysis.relevance_note: Generalized synchronization and conjugacy residuals give an indirect connection, although learned forecasting is the main focus.
analysis.tldr: The authors combine pretrained readouts to reconstruct dynamics beyond training bifurcations. Interpolation theory bounds readout errors and conjugacy residuals; numerical examples demonstrate chaotic extrapolation.
analysis.problem: Extrapolate trained dynamical reconstructions across bifurcations.
analysis.main_result: A generalized-synchronization formula combines existing readouts, with rigorous Lagrange-interpolation bounds on readout error and conjugacy residual. Numerical examples support prediction across bifurcations. The reconstruction assumptions and bounds are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Dynamical reconstruction and reservoir computing.

paper.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
paper.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.

analysis.relevance_note: Dynamical arithmetic averages provide an ergodic-theory connection, while the central target is number-theoretic.
analysis.tldr: The authors extend a dynamical prime-number-theorem generalization to multivariate polynomials of sufficiently large Birch rank. Related results treat integer points on algebraic varieties.
analysis.problem: Obtain dynamical Chowla-type statements for multivariate polynomials and varieties.
analysis.main_result: The extension requires Birch rank sufficiently large in terms of polynomial degree, and analogous averages are established over integer points of algebraic varieties. Neither the rank threshold nor the exact dynamical-average statement is provided. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Dynamical generalizations of arithmetic averaging.

paper.title: Modular Existential Closedness
paper.abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.

analysis.relevance_note: Ratner orbit theorems and homogeneous group actions are explicit tools in this modular-functional application.
analysis.tldr: The author proves Modular Existential Closedness for the reflected modular function. Unipotent orbit structure and a limiting-system construction yield solutions on broad free irreducible varieties.
analysis.problem: Find modular-function points on algebraic varieties under the specified non-overdetermination conditions.
analysis.main_result: For the modular \(j\)-function extended by Schwarz reflection to \(\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R\), every broad free irreducible \(V\subseteq\mathbb C^n\times\mathbb C^n\) contains a point \((\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_n,j(\tau_1),\ldots,j(\tau_n))\) with nonreal \(\tau_i\). Broadness and freeness exclude the stated overdetermination; their exact definitions are not supplied. Not specified in the abstract. The argument uses unipotent orbits to form a simpler limiting system with an isolated solution, then transfers existence to the original system.
analysis.context: Homogeneous dynamics applied to modular functional equations.

paper.title: Finite-step projective dynamics of Schr\"odinger cocycles: non-degeneracy, regularity, and rigidity
paper.abstract: We study the no deterministic images condition (NDI) for Schr\"odinger cocycles, which excludes a common image of a fixed probability measure under almost all projective transfer transformations. We prove two-step NDI at every energy for nonconstant measurable potentials over mixing systems and ergodic potentials with infinite essential range, and classify persistence for finite-state locally constant potentials. For bounded Markov and hidden Markov potentials on general state spaces under a one-step $L^2$ norm gap condition on the Markov operator, we prove H\"older bounds for solution-direction distributions above an exponential cutoff and H\"older conditional stationary measures. Counterexamples show the essential sharpness of both assumptions. For nonconstant real trigonometric potentials, including the almost Mathieu operator, we prove NDI and H\"older bounds for distributions of solution directions at all steps $k\ge2$ and all frequencies (rational or irrational). The exponent depends on the step, while the constant is uniform in steps, frequency and energy on compact intervals. For every irrational frequency and every energy with positive Lyapunov exponent, we prove non-atomicity of both Oseledets direction distributions and convergence to the unstable distribution from every phase-independent initial probability. This gives a new criterion for a zero Lyapunov exponent: a subsequential limit with an atom for one fixed initial direction suffices. All these results extend to an analytic class, with step-dependent regularity bounds.

analysis.relevance_note: Projective cocycles, stationary measures and Lyapunov exponents give a substantial ergodic and spectral connection.
analysis.tldr: The author establishes finite-step nondegeneracy and regularity of Schrödinger solution-direction distributions under several dynamical assumptions. Positive Lyapunov exponents imply nonatomic Oseledets distributions and a convergence result for initial probabilities.
analysis.problem: Study no deterministic images, projective distribution regularity and rigidity for Schrödinger cocycles.
analysis.main_result: Two-step NDI holds at every energy for nonconstant measurable potentials over mixing systems and for ergodic potentials with infinite essential range. Bounded Markov and hidden-Markov potentials satisfying a one-step \(L^2\) norm gap have Hölder bounds above an exponential cutoff and Hölder conditional stationary measures, with counterexamples showing essential sharpness. Nonconstant real trigonometric potentials have NDI and step-dependent Hölder exponents for all steps at least two and all frequencies; constants are uniform as stated on compact energy intervals. At irrational frequencies and positive Lyapunov exponent, both Oseledets distributions are nonatomic and every phase-independent initial probability converges to the unstable distribution. An atomic subsequential limit from a fixed initial direction thus gives a zero-exponent criterion. An analytic extension is also obtained.
methods: Finite-step projective transfer analysis; further proof methods are not stated
analysis.context: Random and quasiperiodic Schrödinger cocycle distributions.

paper.title: Phase response approach to networked neural activity models with delays
paper.abstract: Networks of delay-coupled neural mass models alternate between synchrony and anti-phase locking as the delay between brain regions increases. The origin of these delay-dependent bands has remained unclear. Here, we show that a single function, the phase interaction function $H$ of an isolated node, predicts where the bands occur and explains why they repeat. For a Wilson--Cowan model with intra-nodal delay $\tau$ and inter-nodal delay $\rho$, we compute the limit cycle and phase response, and hence $H$, by harmonic balance. Each band boundary is a zero of $H'$ shifted by the phase lag $\Omega\rho$, so the bands repeat in $\rho$ with the oscillation period. Simulations of the full delay-differential networks confirm these predictions, from two nodes, where predicted frequencies agree to second order in the coupling strength, to rings, where the theory also identifies coexisting stable twisted states that random initial conditions rarely reach. At weak coupling, the delays at which synchrony gains or loses stability are set by the node dynamics alone, whereas stable anti-phase states require a bipartite network. For a macaque connectome, metastability peaks at the edges of the synchrony bands, where the stability margin of phase-locking vanishes. The reduction is accurate for coupling strengths well below the slowest Floquet exponent of the node, beyond which a phase--amplitude description is needed. More broadly, vanishing phase-locking stability provides a simple route to metastability in delay-coupled oscillator networks and a candidate mechanism for the flexible coordination of brain dynamics.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is delay-coupled neural-model synchronization and biological simulations, without a central entropy, dimension or symbolic theme.

paper.title: Arbitrarily Many Primitive Prime Divisors in an Iterate of $x^d+c$
paper.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $R$, let $f_{d,c}(x)=x^d+c\in K[x]$ be a unicritical polynomial of degree $d\ge2$, and let $\varrho_d(n,c)$ denote the number of primitive prime divisors of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$, the $n$-th term of the critical orbit of $f_{d,c}$. We show that $\varrho_d(n,c)$ admits no uniform bound, that is, no bound depending only on $d$ and $n$. More precisely, for all $n\ge1$ and $t\ge1$ there is $c\in R$ for which $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ has at least $t$ primitive prime divisors, and these primes may be prescribed to occur with any given multiplicities. This can be done simultaneously for any finite set of iterates. The construction rests on a density computation. Namely, the set of primes occurring as a primitive prime divisor of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ for some $c$ has positive density. We compute that density explicitly for $d=2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, under a hypothesis on the Galois group of the associated Gleason polynomial, verified for $n\le16$. As an application, we produce, for every $m\ge1$, a parameter $c\in R$ (in fact, a whole residue class of them), for which the splitting field of $f_{d,c}^m(x)$ has the maximal possible degree over $K$.

analysis.relevance_note: Critical polynomial orbits give an arithmetic-dynamics connection, though prime divisors are the main target.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct parameters whose specified critical iterates have arbitrarily many primitive prime divisors with prescribed multiplicities. Positive prime density supports the construction, with explicit conditional computations in a quadratic case.
analysis.problem: Determine whether primitive-prime counts of unicritical critical iterates admit a degree-and-iterate-only bound.
analysis.main_result: For \(x^d+c\), \(d\geq2\), over a number field with integer ring \(R\), every \(n,t\geq1\) admits \(c\in R\) with at least \(t\) primitive prime divisors of the critical iterate, with prescribed multiplicities; this can be simultaneous for finitely many iterates. Relevant primes have positive density. For quadratics over the rationals the density is computed under a Gleason-polynomial Galois hypothesis verified through iterate sixteen. For every iteration depth, a whole parameter residue class gives maximal possible splitting-field degree.
methods: Positive-density computation for primitive prime divisors
analysis.context: Unicritical arithmetic dynamics and prime divisors.

paper.title: Convergence of Quantum Lindstedt Series and Semiclassical Renormalization
paper.abstract: In this work we consider the KAM renormalizability problem for small pseudodifferential perturbations of the semiclassical isochronous transport operator with Diophantine frequencies on the torus. Assuming that the symbol of the perturbation is real analytic and globally bounded, we prove convergence of the quantum Lindstedt series and describe completely the set of semiclassical measures and quantum limits of the renormalized system. Each of these measures is given by symplectic deformation of the Haar measure on an invariant torus for the unperturbed classical system.

analysis.relevance_note: Semiclassical measures as deformed invariant-torus Haar measures give a clear invariant-measure and Hamiltonian connection.
analysis.tldr: The author proves convergence of a quantum Lindstedt series for small analytic bounded perturbations of torus transport. All semiclassical measures and quantum limits of the renormalized system are described as deformed torus Haar measures.
analysis.problem: Solve a semiclassical KAM renormalizability problem and classify its measure limits.
analysis.main_result: For small pseudodifferential perturbations of the semiclassical isochronous transport operator on a torus with Diophantine frequencies, a real-analytic globally bounded perturbation symbol yields a convergent quantum Lindstedt series. Every resulting semiclassical measure and quantum limit is a symplectic deformation of Haar measure on an unperturbed invariant torus. The smallness threshold is not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Symplectic deformation of torus Haar measures
analysis.context: Semiclassical KAM theory and invariant-torus limits.

paper.title: Comparing Periodic Point Invariants for Parameterized Families of Maps
paper.abstract: We compare different periodic point invariants for families of maps parameterized over a compact manifold. Malkiewich and Ponto showed that, in the case of a single map, the Fuller trace is equivalent to the collection of Reidmeister traces of iterates. In this paper, we show that, in contrast to the case of a single map, the fiberwise Fuller trace is a strictly more sensitive invariant than the collection of fiberwise Reidemeister traces of iterates. This resolves a conjecture of Malkiewich and Ponto. We also prove that our construction gives a geometric representation of elements of the kernel of the ghost map out of topological restriction homology.

analysis.relevance_note: Periodic-point invariants for parameterized dynamics directly connect topology and dynamical classification.
analysis.tldr: The author proves that fiberwise Fuller traces detect strictly more than fiberwise Reidemeister traces of all iterates for parameter families. The construction also geometrically represents a specified ghost-map kernel.
analysis.problem: Compare periodic-point invariants of map families over compact manifolds.
analysis.main_result: Unlike the single-map equivalence, for families parameterized by a compact manifold the fiberwise Fuller trace is strictly more sensitive than the collection of fiberwise Reidemeister traces of iterates, resolving the cited conjecture. The construction represents elements of the kernel of the ghost map out of topological restriction homology. Specific examples and construction details are not stated. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Geometric representation of ghost-map kernel elements; further construction details are not stated
analysis.context: Parameterized periodic-point theory and topological traces.

paper.title: Lubin's conjecture for height-one $p$-adic dynamical systems over $p(p-1)$-tame extensions
paper.abstract: We prove Lubin's conjecture for height-one commuting pairs of formal power series defined over the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}$ of finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ whose ramification index is coprime to $p(p-1)$. For such a pair $(f, u)$, with $f$ noninvertible and $u$ invertible, we show that $(f, u)$ is a pair of endomorphisms of a formal group defined over $\mathcal{O}$. The proof relies on extracting a crystalline character of weight $1$ from the Galois set $T_f$ of $f$-consistent sequences, using it to define a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module structure on $T_f$ for which $f$ is an endomorphism, and applying explicit functors in integral $p$-adic Hodge theory to recover the latent formal group.

analysis.relevance_note: Commuting formal dynamics and formal-group rigidity give an arithmetic-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The author proves the stated height-one Lubin conjecture over finite local-field extensions with a coprime ramification condition. Commuting invertible and noninvertible series become endomorphisms of a common formal group.
analysis.problem: Recover a latent formal group from a height-one commuting pair of formal power series.
analysis.main_result: Over the integer ring \(\mathcal O\) of a finite extension of \(\mathbb Q_p\) whose ramification index is coprime to \(p(p-1)\), a height-one pair \((f,u)\), with \(f\) noninvertible and \(u\) invertible, consists of endomorphisms of a formal group over \(\mathcal O\).
methods: Extraction of a weight-one crystalline character
Explicit functors in integral p-adic Hodge theory
analysis.context: Local arithmetic dynamics and formal groups.

paper.title: Optimality and annealing path planning of dynamical analog solvers
paper.abstract: Recently proposed analog solvers based on dynamical systems, such as Ising machines, are promising platforms for large-scale combinatorial optimization. Yet, given the heuristic nature of the field, there is very limited insight on optimality guarantees of the solvers, as well as how parameter schedules shape dynamics and outcomes. Here, we develop a dynamical mean-field framework to analyze Ising-machine dynamics for finding the ground state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick(SK) model of spin glasses and identify mechanisms that enable rapid convergence to provenly near-optimal energies. For a fixed target energy density Ec, we show that solutions are typically reached within O(1) matrix vector multiplications, indicating constant time complexity. We further delineate theoretical limitations arising from different parameter-scheduling trajectories and demonstrate a pronounced benefit of temperature-only annealing for the Coherent Ising Machine. Building on these insights, we propose a general framework for designing optimized parameter schedules, thereby improving the practical effectiveness of Ising machines for complex optimization tasks. The superior performance of the dynamical solvers is illustrated by the attainment of the ground state energy of the SK model.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is analog optimization solvers and scheduling for spin-glass energies rather than the central dynamical invariants in the profile.

paper.title: Formulation and Learning Of The Forecasting Problem
paper.abstract: Machine learning has opened new frontiers in purely data-driven forecasting of dynamical systems; the resulting methods are showing considerable promise in some application domains. However, in contrast to model-driven algorithms, analysis of these data-driven methods is poorly developed. In this paper we address this issue, developing a theory to underpin data-driven methods to solve forecasting problems. The theoretical framework comprises two key components: (i) establishing the existence of a mapping defining the forecasting problem; (ii) showing that it is possible to approximate this mapping by supervised learning techniques, to arbitrary accuracy. We work in the continuous-time and noise-free setting as this defines a simple canonical setting in which to establish an underpinning theory; the continuous-time setting leads to an operator formulation of the problem in which the underlying forecasting map is defined on pathspace. As a byproduct of our framework we show that analogous existence and approximation results may be obtained for the smoothing problem of recovering unobserved components of dynamical systems, from observed components, using supervised learning. The theoretical results, for both forecasting and smoothing, are illustrated with experiments studying the Lorenz `63, Lorenz `96 and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamical systems.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is existence and supervised approximation of forecasting operators, without central entropy, fractal or symbolic-dynamics content.

paper.title: Canonical separating coordinates in the generalized cubic H\'enon-Heiles systems
paper.abstract: We study the three classical integrable generalized cubic H\'enon--Heiles systems -- Kaup--Kupershmidt, KdV$_5$, and Sawada--Kotera -- from the viewpoint of bi-Hamiltonian geometry and separation of variables. On the standard symplectic manifold $T^*\mathbb R^2$, we construct compatible Poisson deformations $P_1=L_XP_0$, compute the associated recursion operators $N=P_1P_0^{-1}$, and analyze the action of $N^*$ on the codistribution generated by the first integrals. This yields the corresponding control matrices, whose eigenvalues provide the separating coordinates. For the generalized Kaup--Kupershmidt case we carry out the construction explicitly: we determine a deformation vector field, the compatible Poisson tensor, the torsionless recursion operator, the control matrix, the separating coordinates, and, crucially, the conjugate momenta. We then derive the separated relations and write the Hamilton equations in canonical separated variables, thus decomposing the original Hamiltonian system into two separated subsystems. To the best of our knowledge, this explicit derivation of the separating variables and, in particular, of the conjugate momenta for the generalized Kaup--Kupershmidt system is new. For the KdV$_5$ and Sawada--Kotera cases we show how the same bi-Hamiltonian scheme applies, emphasizing both the common geometric mechanism and the features peculiar to each system. In this way, the three generalized cubic H\'enon--Heiles systems are treated within a unified framework based on compatible Poisson structures, recursion operators, control matrices, and Darboux--Nijenhuis coordinates.

analysis.relevance_note: Poisson and symplectic geometry of integrability provides an indirect geometric-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors treat three integrable cubic Hénon--Heiles families through a common bi-Hamiltonian separation scheme. They explicitly derive separating coordinates and conjugate momenta in the generalized Kaup--Kupershmidt case.
analysis.problem: Construct canonical separating variables using compatible Poisson structures.
analysis.main_result: Compatible Poisson deformations, recursion operators and their action on first-integral codistributions yield control matrices whose eigenvalues separate variables. The generalized Kaup--Kupershmidt construction explicitly includes momenta, separated relations and canonical Hamilton equations, decomposing the system into two subsystems. The same scheme treats the KdV-five and Sawada--Kotera cases. No entropy or invariant-measure conclusion is asserted.
analysis.context: Bi-Hamiltonian geometry of integrable Hénon--Heiles systems.

paper.title: $T$-admissible processes and noncommutative weighted ergodic theorems
paper.abstract: In this article, we study the bilaterally almost uniform (b.a.u.) convergence of weighted averages of a positive Dunford-Schwartz operator $T$ acting on the noncommutative $L_p$-spaces $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ associated to a semifinite von Neumann algebra $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$ for a variety of sequences which includes those generated by bounded i.i.d. sequences, the M\"{o}bius function, the Liouville function, and totally balanced automatic sequences. If $1<p<\infty$, then sequences generated by i.i.d. sequences with finite $q$-th moment for $q=\frac{p}{p-1}$ being the H\"{o}lder conjugate of $p$ are also shown to generate good weights for $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We also study similar problems for $T$-admissible processes on a semifinite von Neumann algebra, showing that if a Wiener-Wintner type ergodic theorem holds for a class $\mathcal{W}\subset W_q$ of weights, then it also holds for strongly $p$-bounded $T$-admissible processes assuming that the duality $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$ holds and that $T$ is a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism. A version of this result for arbitrary positive Dunford-Schwartz operators is also considered.

analysis.relevance_note: Weighted noncommutative ergodic convergence gives a substantial ergodic-theory connection.
analysis.tldr: The author proves weighted bilaterally almost-uniform ergodic convergence for positive Dunford--Schwartz operators. A transfer result treats strongly bounded admissible processes under a Wiener--Wintner hypothesis.
analysis.problem: Establish good weights and process versions of noncommutative weighted ergodic theorems.
analysis.main_result: For semifinite noncommutative \(L_p\), \(1\leq p<\infty\), weights include bounded IID sequences, Möbius, Liouville and totally balanced automatic sequences. For \(1<p<\infty\), IID weights with finite conjugate \(q=p/(p-1)\) moment are also good. A Wiener--Wintner theorem for a weight class transfers to strongly \(p\)-bounded admissible processes under conjugate duality when the operator is a normal trace-preserving star-automorphism. A version for arbitrary positive Dunford--Schwartz operators is considered; precise additional conclusions are not given. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Transfer from Wiener--Wintner weighted theorems to admissible processes; further proof methods are not stated
analysis.context: Noncommutative weighted ergodic theory.

paper.title: SpectONet: A Physics-Guided Spectral Deep Operator Network for Euler-Bernoulli Beam Dynamics
paper.abstract: This paper proposes a novel physics-guided spectral deep operator network, termed SpectONet, for solving Euler-Bernoulli beam (EBB) vibration problems. The proposed framework integrates the operator-learning capability of DeepONet with physics-informed constraints and Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto (CGL) sensor placement. Unlike conventional DeepONet frameworks, which commonly employ uniformly distributed sensors, SpectONet uses nonuniform spectral sensor locations with a higher concentration of points near the domain boundaries. This sampling strategy improves the finite-dimensional representation of boundary-sensitive structural responses while requiring only a limited number of branch-network inputs. The governing beam equation, together with the associated initial and boundary conditions, is incorporated into the training objective to promote physically consistent and generalizable predictions. Numerical experiments on three EBB vibration problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Comparisons with strong baseline models such as Vanilla DeepONet, PI-DeepONet, PINN, and CNN-UNet show that SpectONet consistently achieves lower prediction errors across all considered evaluation metrics. In particular, SpectONet achieves an average reduction of approximately 79% in the mean relative $\mathcal{L}_2$ error compared with the best-performing baseline across the three benchmark problems. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SpectONet as an accurate physics-guided operator-learning framework for structural vibration analysis.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is engineering operator learning for beam vibrations, without a central entropy, dimension or topological-dynamics theme.

paper.title: Two averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
paper.abstract: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. In 1965, Chowla gave a conjecture that the values of $\lambda(n+h_1),\dots, \lambda(n+h_k)$ are asymptotically unrelated for any distinct natural numbers $h_1, \dots, h_k$. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will show a dynamical generalization of Chowla's conjecture on average. In the proof, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. Moreover, we will use this approach to show an analogue of the dynamical Chowla's conjecture along the primes on average. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and a variant for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.

analysis.relevance_note: Dynamical arithmetic averages give an ergodic-theory connection, with an explicitly averaged scope.
analysis.tldr: The author establishes averaged dynamical Chowla generalizations, including a prime analogue. Further results dynamically extend a logarithmic two-point theorem and a sum-of-digits composition variant.
analysis.problem: Extend arithmetic correlation statements to averaged dynamical formulations.
analysis.main_result: The claims are dynamical generalizations on average, including along primes, together with a dynamical extension of Tao’s logarithmic two-point theorem and a variant for composing a sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function. They do not assert the full unaveraged Chowla conjecture. The precise averages and assumptions are not specified. Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Adaptation of the cited Qi--Zheng approach
Use of the cited Charamaras--Richter framework
analysis.context: Averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla-type statements.

paper.title: A characterization of the reversibility of linear cellular automata
paper.abstract: Let $G$ be a group, let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field, and let $V$ be a $\mathbb{K}$-vector space. We prove that there exists a bijective linear cellular automaton $V^G\to V^G$ whose inverse is not a cellular automaton if and only if $G$ is not locally finite and $\dim_{\mathbb{K}}V \geq |\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$. In particular, $|\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$ is the exact dimension threshold for non-reversibility. This answers an open problem proposed by T. Ceccherini-Silberstein and M. Coornaert.

analysis.relevance_note: Reversibility of group cellular automata directly matches symbolic dynamics and group actions.
analysis.tldr: The author characterizes exactly when a bijective linear cellular automaton can fail to have a cellular inverse. The threshold depends on local finiteness of the group and the vector-space dimension.
analysis.problem: Determine existence of nonreversible bijective linear cellular automata.
analysis.main_result: For a group \(G\), field \(\mathbb K\) and vector space \(V\), a bijective linear cellular automaton on \(V^G\) with noncellular inverse exists exactly when \(G\) is not locally finite and \(\dim_{\mathbb K}V\geq|\mathbb K|^{\aleph_0}\). This is the exact stated dimension threshold. The proof method is not given. Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Reversibility in linear group cellular dynamics.
